```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Databricks is a hosted data and analytics platform. Its SQL warehouses run
queries against your tables. Query a Databricks SQL warehouse from Shiny using each visitor's Databricks
account. `oauth_db_databricks()` gives you a DBI connection for SQL or
dbplyr queries.

The same sign-in works with brickster's API functions, including warehouse
listing and query submission.

For guided setup and an editable app, run
`shinyOAuthDB::oauth_db_cloud_demo("databricks")`. The
[cloud demo guide](cloud-demos.html) explains the console prompts,
warehouse selection and Free Edition's registration limitation.

## Register the app

In R, run `install.packages("brickster")` and ask your administrator to
[register a Databricks OAuth application](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/integrations/enable-disable-oauth)
with a client secret and `http://localhost:8100` as its redirect URI.
Allow the scopes requested by the preset, including `all-apis` and
`offline_access`. Users need access to the workspace, warehouse, and data.

Save the client ID and secret in a local `.Renviron` file and restart R:

```text
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret
```

In the Databricks **account console**, an administrator opens **Settings >
App connections > Add connection**. Register `http://localhost:8100`, allow
**All APIs** for this preset and generate a client secret. Copy the ID and
secret from the result; the secret can't be retrieved later. These are
[custom OAuth connections](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/integrations/enable-disable-oauth),
separate from service-principal machine credentials.

| App value | Where to find it |
| --- | --- |
| `host` | Your workspace browser address, e.g. `example.cloud.databricks.com` |
| `warehouse_id` | Workspace **SQL Warehouses > your warehouse > Connection details**; also the last part of its HTTP path |
| Client ID and secret | The account console's custom app connection |

Give users **CAN USE** on the warehouse and the appropriate catalog, schema
and table privileges. The cloud service can't be reproduced by a local
Docker demo.

## A complete app

Save this as `example.R`. Replace the workspace host and copy the warehouse ID
from the warehouse's connection details:

```{r app}
library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

host <- "example.cloud.databricks.com"
client <- oauth_db_databricks_client(
  host = host,
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100"
)

ui <- oauth_ui(
  fluidPage(
    actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
    actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
    tableOutput("rows")
  ),
  id = "auth",
  client = client
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server("auth", client, auto_redirect = FALSE)
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  con <- oauth_db_databricks(
    auth$connection,
    host = host,
    warehouse_id = "warehouse-id"
  )

  output$rows <- renderTable({
    connection <- con()
    DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT current_user()")
  })
}

runApp(
  shinyApp(ui, server, uiPattern = ".*"),
  port = 8100,
  launch.browser = FALSE
)

# Open the app in your regular browser at http://localhost:8100
# (viewers in RStudio/Positron/etc. cannot perform necessary redirects)
```

Run `source("example.R")` and open
`http://localhost:8100`. Sign in to run the query; signing out clears the
output.

The query shows the Databricks user. Replace it with SQL for your tables.
For dbplyr, get `connection <- con()` first, then pass it to
`dplyr::tbl()`.

## Call brickster functions

To list warehouses, add `verbatimTextOutput("warehouses")` to the UI
and this code inside `server()`:

```{r warehouses}
databricks <- oauth_db_databricks_api(auth$connection, host = host)

output$warehouses <- renderPrint({
  databricks$call(brickster::db_sql_warehouse_list)
})
```

Pass the function and its usual arguments to `$call()`. The client
supplies the workspace host and the user's current token.

For example, to use brickster's query API, replace the table output with
`verbatimTextOutput("rows")` and the render expression with:

```{r api-query}
output$rows <- renderPrint({
  databricks$call(
    brickster::db_sql_query,
    warehouse_id = "warehouse-id",
    statement = "SELECT current_user()",
    disposition = "INLINE",
    show_progress = FALSE
  )
})
```

This returns brickster's query result. Use the DBI helper above when you
want `DBI::dbGetQuery()` to return a data frame.

## Connection options

Supply `http_path = "/sql/1.0/warehouses/warehouse-id"` instead of
`warehouse_id` if you have the HTTP path. Set `catalog` and `schema`
to choose SQL defaults; other connection options go to brickster.

Call `con()` before each operation. When its token changes, the helper
replaces the connection. On sign-out or session end, `con()` stops returning
the connection and calls the driver's cleanup method. The brickster driver
doesn't invalidate retained native handles: a saved connection can still
submit requests with its copied token. Keep using `con()` for each operation.
See [Authentication and sessions](authorization.html) for results saved in
the app.

## Azure Databricks with Entra sign-in

For a workspace that accepts Microsoft Entra tokens, use an Entra Web app
registration with delegated Databricks access. Set `OAUTHDB_TENANT_ID`
and replace the client with:

```{r entra-client}
client <- oauth_db_microsoft_client(
  services = "databricks_entra",
  tenant_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_TENANT_ID"),
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100"
)
```

Change `host` to the Azure workspace hostname and set
`auth_mode = "entra"` on both `oauth_db_databricks()` and
`oauth_db_databricks_api()`.
